modules.title: How to Read and Argue
modules.intro: The classical tools for reading and arguing: definition, the syllogism, the common fallacies, and the geometric proof. These are enough to follow the arguments in every later module. (The art of the speech itself is learned in Rome, with the Rhetorica ad Herennium.)
takeaways: Classification comes before argument. Genus, species, and difference are the basis of a definition.
A syllogism is valid because of its form, whatever its content. Fallacies are arguments that only look valid.
Euclid's method of building from axioms became the model of certain knowledge.

modules.title: Homer and the Gods
modules.intro: The Iliad and the Odyssey are the most frequently referenced works in the Western sections of the list. This module reads the books that carry each poem's plot and turning points, plus Hesiod's account of the gods and the earliest Greek lyric.
takeaways: The Iliad is about the anger of Achilles, and about honor, mortality, and recognizing a shared humanity in an enemy (Priam and Achilles in Book 24).
The Odyssey is about cunning, homecoming, and xenia, the obligations between guest and host.
Hesiod gives the family tree of the gods and a moral picture of justice and labor.

modules.title: Tragedy, History, and the City
modules.intro: Athens in the fifth century BC produced tragedy, comedy, and history writing within a few decades. Read two tragedians, one comedy, and the founding passages of the two founding historians.
takeaways: Tragedy stages conflicts that have no clean resolution: vengeance against justice, family against the law of the city.
Herodotus explains events through custom and fortune. Thucydides explains them through power, fear, and interest.
The Melian dialogue is the classic statement of 'the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must'.

modules.title: Plato and Aristotle
modules.intro: The two philosophers whose questions set the agenda for the rest of the list: what justice is, what the soul is, what a good life is, and how we know anything. The passages below are the ones later writers quote most often.
takeaways: Plato: justice is an order in the soul and the city. True knowledge is of the Forms, and the Cave allegory shows the path from opinion to knowledge.
Aristotle: the good life is activity in accordance with virtue, virtue is a mean found by practical wisdom, and humans are political animals.
Heraclitus and Parmenides frame the question of change and permanence that both men answer.

works.author: Porphyry
works.title: Isagoge
works.read: The whole text; it is short. Learn the five predicables.
works.edition: Tr. Jonathan Barnes, Porphyry: Introduction (Oxford Clarendon Later Ancient Philosophers)

works.author: Aristotle
works.title: Categories
works.read: Chapters 1-5, ending with the account of substance.
works.edition: Tr. J.L. Ackrill, Categories and De Interpretatione (Oxford Clarendon Aristotle Series); also in The Complete Works of Aristotle, ed. Barnes (Princeton)

works.author: Aristotle
works.title: the rest of the Organon
works.read: Prior Analytics I.1-7 (the syllogism) and Sophistical Refutations 4-5 (the thirteen fallacies).
works.edition: The Complete Works of Aristotle, ed. Jonathan Barnes, vol. 1 (Princeton); Prior Analytics tr. Robin Smith (Hackett)

works.author: Euclid
works.title: Elements
works.read: Book I: definitions, postulates, common notions, then propositions 1-5 and 47 (the Pythagorean theorem).
works.edition: Tr. T.L. Heath, The Thirteen Books of the Elements (Dover); Green Lion Press one-volume edition

works.author: Homer
works.title: The Iliad
works.edition: Iliad tr. Richmond Lattimore (Chicago) or Robert Fagles (Penguin); Odyssey tr. Lattimore (Harper) or Emily Wilson (Norton)

works.author: Hesiod
works.title: Theogony
works.read: Theogony 1-210 (creation and Kronos) and Works and Days 1-201 (Prometheus, Pandora, the five ages).
works.edition: Tr. M.L. West, Theogony and Works and Days (Oxford World's Classics)

works.author: Sappho
works.title: Fragments
works.edition: Tr. Anne Carson, If Not, Winter (Vintage)

works.author: Aeschylus
works.title: The Oresteia
works.read: Agamemnon and The Eumenides, the first and last plays of the trilogy.
works.edition: Tr. Richmond Lattimore, in The Complete Greek Tragedies (Chicago); or tr. Robert Fagles (Penguin)

works.author: Sophocles
works.title: The Theban Plays
works.edition: Tr. Robert Fagles, The Three Theban Plays (Penguin); or David Grene, Sophocles I (Chicago)

works.author: Euripides
works.title: The Tragedies
works.edition: The Complete Greek Tragedies: Euripides, ed. Grene and Lattimore (Chicago)

works.author: Aristophanes
works.title: The Comedies
works.read: The Clouds, a comic portrait of Socrates.
works.edition: Tr. Peter Meineck, Clouds (Hackett); or Alan Sommerstein, Lysistrata and Other Plays (Penguin)

works.author: Herodotus
works.title: The Histories
works.read: The preface and I.1-45 (Croesus and Solon); VII.201-239 (Thermopylae).
works.edition: The Landmark Herodotus, ed. Robert Strassler, tr. Andrea Purvis (Anchor)

works.author: Thucydides
works.title: The Peloponnesian War
works.read: I.20-23 (method); II.35-54 (Funeral Oration and plague); III.82-83 (civil strife at Corcyra); V.84-116 (the Melian dialogue).
works.edition: The Landmark Thucydides, ed. Robert Strassler, tr. Richard Crawley (Free Press)

works.title: The Pre-Socratics
works.read: The fragments of Heraclitus and of Parmenides only.
works.edition: Ed. and tr. Jonathan Barnes, Early Greek Philosophy (Penguin); or Kirk, Raven and Schofield, The Presocratic Philosophers (Cambridge)

works.author: Plato
works.title: Republic
works.read: The Apology (not on the list) as a preface. Republic I-II (Thrasymachus and the Ring of Gyges), IV (the parts of the soul), VI.507-VII.521 (sun, line, cave), X.614-621 (Myth of Er). Symposium 201d-212c (Diotima). Phaedo 115-118 (the death of Socrates).
works.edition: Plato: Complete Works, ed. John M. Cooper (Hackett). Republic tr. Allan Bloom (Basic Books) or Grube/Reeve (Hackett)

works.author: Aristotle
works.title: Nicomachean Ethics
works.read: Nicomachean Ethics I, II, and X.6-8. Politics I.1-2. Poetics 6-14 (tragedy).
works.edition: Nicomachean Ethics tr. Terence Irwin (Hackett) or Bartlett and Collins (Chicago); Politics tr. C.D.C. Reeve (Hackett); Poetics tr. Joe Sachs (Focus)
